header.tagline: Audio + Video Cue Playback for Live Events

seo.description: Audio and video cue playback for live events, with One Shots, Show Mode, dedicated Video Output, and true-peak protection.

hero.title: Make the next cue feel inevitable.
hero.lede: Prepare audio and video cues for live shows. Keep the control surface calm, the audience output visible, and the next sound one touch away.

signal.localFirstText: Play from the machine you trust — or connect to a stage-side server.
signal.platformsText: Windows, macOS, and Linux builds with dedicated video output.

workflow.title: Prepare once. Perform clearly.
workflow.intro: Build the show, check the signal, and keep the live surface focused — with audio, video, and remote control in one workflow.
workflow.step1Text: Bring in local audio/video, YouTube, or selected Spotify tracks, then order them into nested playlist groups.
workflow.step2Text: Shape each cue with peak/RMS waveforms, markers, fades, loudness or true-peak normalization, routing, and optional LTC timecode.
workflow.step3Text: Use Preview, One Shots, keyboard/MIDI controls, Show Mode, and live meters without losing the next cue.

oneShots.screenshotAlt: DonWells Cue One Shots panel with permanent cells ready for quick playback
oneShots.title: Keep the important sounds one touch away.
oneShots.text: One Shots are a permanent quick-play surface for announcements, stings, effects, walk-ons, and beds. In Show Mode, arm a cell before firing it from the tile, a hotkey, or MIDI, while the source playlist stays untouched.
oneShots.point1: Copy local files or playlist cues into a cell without changing the source.
oneShots.point2: Arm a cell for deliberate firing from its tile, hotkey, or MIDI controller.
oneShots.point3: Duck or replace program playback, set retrigger behavior, and keep countdowns visible.

showMode.screenshotAlt: DonWells Cue Show Mode with a simplified playlist and live output meters
showMode.title: Less interface when the room is live.
showMode.text: Switch to a simplified, touch-friendly playback view for the performance. The shortcuts bar, Preview panel, current/next cues, and meters stay close while edit-only controls step out of the way.

safety.title: Protect the signal. Keep the picture ready.
safety.text: Preview keeps auditioning off the program bus; Output Target, normalization, and true-peak limiting keep levels deliberate; Video Output gives the audience a dedicated picture surface.
safety.item1Text: Audition, seek, trim, and set the next cue through a dedicated monitor output.
safety.item2Text: Match broadcast, streaming, radio, OTT, or live-console targets before the cue reaches air.
safety.item3Text: Send H.264/HEVC video to a selected display, with Identify Displays, a test card, standby image, and recovery controls.
safety.item4Text: In Show Mode, require an explicit arm before a cell can fire; leaving Show Mode disarms cells, while Stop is always available.
safety.videoProofText: Send H.264/HEVC picture to a selected display while audio stays on the normal engine path.

precision.title: Shape the moment.
precision.intro: Trim the entrance. Shape the fade. Set the handoff. Turn a folder of media into a sequence that feels considered.
precision.screenshotAlt: DonWells Cue cue playback editor with waveform, in and out markers, fade controls, and loudness settings
precision.inText: Move the cue start without rewriting the source media.
precision.outText: Define the end point the operator will actually rehearse.
precision.fadesText: Set fade-in and fade-out shape and duration around those boundaries.
precision.nextText: Place the handoff marker where the next cue should begin, then confirm its end behavior.
precision.loudnessText: Analyze peak, RMS, integrated LUFS, and true peak; apply normalization only after choosing the intended target.
precision.operatorNoteText: Rehearse your trims, fades, loops, and transitions on the hardware you’ll use for the show.

show.title: Less setup. More show.
show.intro: Show Mode puts current playback and the next cue front and center. Try the silent sequence below: press GO and see each cue take its place.
show.keyboardHint: Try it with your keyboard: focus GO, then press Enter or Space.
show.transportAlt: DonWells Cue transport showing Stop All Cues, active cue information, and Play Next target
show.distinctionOne: Selected is the row being inspected.
show.distinctionTwo: Up Next is the engine-acknowledged target.
show.distinctionThree: Active is already playing. Always read the cue name beside Play Next before GO.

oneShots.title: One touch. Its own moment.
oneShots.intro: One Shots are independent quick-play copies for announcements, walk-ons, effects, and beds. In Show Mode, arm the cell before firing it.
oneShots.modeLabel: Choose how a One Shot meets program playback
oneShots.overlayText: Use Overlay when the One Shot should play over current program cues. Check the combined level at the real destination.
oneShots.duckTitle: Set the program to a rehearsed level while the One Shot plays.
oneShots.duckText: Duck Program temporarily sets other active cues to the configured absolute Program Level, then restores their prior gains. Rehearse the return, not just the entrance.
oneShots.replaceTitle: Stop other program cues when the One Shot fires.
oneShots.replaceText: Choose Replace Program when a sound should take over. Other active program cues receive a stop command as the One Shot starts.

oneShots.safetyText: Leaving Show Mode disarms One Shot cells. Stop remains available. A hotkey or MIDI trigger does not remove the need to verify the armed state.

projects.title: Your show. Your setup.
projects.intro: Run the controller and engine on one computer, or connect over a trusted LAN to an engine beside the sound system. The controller shows state; audio still leaves the engine computer.
projects.localText: The desktop controller and audio engine run on the same show machine.
projects.lanText: Connect to the engine computer with its host, port, and token. Treat the network as trusted: control uses token-authenticated HTTP, not an encrypted public-internet transport.
projects.portableText: Keep each show in a dedicated folder: .dwcue stores its state beside media/, and .dwcuepack packages that folder. Verify externally linked media separately.
projects.autosaveTitle: Save the work. Take the show.
projects.autosaveText: Use Autosave while you work, save milestones deliberately, and keep a rehearsal copy before moving to the show machine.
projects.connectionAlt: DonWells Cue server connection settings with host, port, and access token fields
projects.importCaption: Media import options · Copy and duplicate handling · Manual capture 2.6.14
projects.importAlt: DonWells Cue Import Media dialog with project-copy and duplicate-handling choices
projects.caveatText: Remote control belongs on a trusted, private show network. Confirm routing and media readiness on the engine computer before doors open.

docs.title: A little help. Right on cue.
docs.intro: Open the complete operator edition for first-run setup, cue preparation, output checks, remote operation, recovery procedures, and printable show-day checklists.
docs.editionNote: The PDF and interface captures are from operator edition 2.6.14, captured on 6 September 2026. Current installers are available above.
docs.faqOneQuestion: How do I listen before the audience does?
docs.faqOneAnswer: Use Preview with a separate headphone or monitor output. Set and test that route first: if Preview shares the Main speakers, it will be audible to the audience.
docs.faqTwoQuestion: How do I know which cue is next?
docs.faqTwoAnswer: Read the cue named beside Play Next. Up Next is the engine-acknowledged target; selecting a row for inspection does not set it as Up Next.
docs.faqThreeQuestion: What video can I send to the screen?
docs.faqThreeAnswer: Video Output supports H.264 and HEVC on one dedicated audience picture surface. Use Identify Displays and the test card to check the destination. It is not a layered video mixer and has no dedicated blackout control.
docs.faqFourQuestion: Can I control an engine on another computer?
docs.faqFourAnswer: Yes—connect over a trusted LAN using the engine host, port, and access token. Audio leaves the engine computer. Control uses HTTP, so keep this service off the public internet.
docs.faqFiveQuestion: What moves a show between computers?
docs.faqFiveAnswer: Use .dwcuepack to package the dedicated project folder. Copied project media travels with it; verify externally linked media separately and keep the original .dwcue show folder intact.
